title: the same six implicit invocation forms over callees that reach no capability record an empty row, so the program compiles with no layer and runs
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Inference': 'Calling a function with unsatisfied requirements MUST add those capabilities to the caller's R row.' A callee with no requirements adds none, whatever syntax reached it. This is the over-correction guard for `an-invocation-with-no-call-expression-still-charges-its-row`: that case requires a backend to start charging six new invocation forms, and the cheap way to satisfy it is to charge the FORM — every tagged template, every `new`, every `for-of` — rather than the callee it resolves to. This file is what that costs. The module deliberately declares a capability AND a function that reads it (`unused`), so a rule that charges a form because a capability is in scope, or because some function in the module reads one, has something to over-fire on. Nothing calls `unused`, so the correct answer for all six lines is an empty row. THE ORACLE IS THE RUN TIME, and that was measured rather than assumed: `SMITHERS2102` fires on top-level CALLS and every function here is reached through `main`, which the harness calls, so a wrongly charged row is not refused — it aborts, with `Panic: capability 'Db' was not provided` on the reference and `Panic: unsatisfied Context requirement` on the fork, exit code 1 on both. The printed lines are what say each form actually ran and produced its own value: `xT` is the tag's return rather than the raw template, `C` and `B` come from two different constructors so the implicit-super line cannot be satisfied by the explicit one, and the three `ab`s come from `for-of`, a spread and a `yield*` over the same plain array. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: coercion positions and decorators, for the same reasons its refusal sibling omits them — a shared negative that also covered those families would go red for their defects and be read as an invocation-form regression. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the first declared stdout line from `xT` to `xTT` turns the case red on BOTH backends with the stdout diff printed, and the expectation was restored byte-identically (sha256 0c22483952c9592500429b8503b64c33e5262a17b0557476791a0f2434013f6a before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently).
